title: Multiplying 3-Digit by 2-Digit Numbers
seo_title: Grade 5 Multiplying 3-Digit by 2-Digit Numbers Worksheets (TEKS 5.3B, STAAR)
standard_text: 5.3B multiply with fluency a three-digit number by a two-digit number using the standard algorithm
meta_desc: Free Grade 5 multiplication worksheets for Texas TEKS 5.3B: 3-digit by 2-digit multiplication with the standard algorithm, partial products, numbers with zeros and word problems. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Multiply by the ones, then by the tens (write a 0), then add.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • In the standard algorithm, multiply the top number by the ones digit, then by the tens digit (write a 0 first), then add the two partial products.
  • Regroup carefully in each row, and cross out regrouped digits before the next row.
  • Estimate first to check: 467 × 32 is about 500 × 30 = 15,000.

Examples

Example

467 × 32

467 × 2 = 934

467 × 30 = 14,010

934 + 14,010

Answer: 14,944

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Forgetting the 0 in the second rowThe tens digit stands for tens: 467 × 30, not 467 × 3.
Adding a regrouped digit twiceUse each regrouped digit once, then cross it out.
Lining up the partial products wronglyLine up by place value before adding.

faq.a: We are multiplying by tens, so every product is a multiple of 10.

faq.q: How can I check my product?
